data.narrative:
Asylon Robotics is a Series B-stage autonomous systems company in the Drones & Autonomous sector, having raised $40M to date. The comp universe for this stage is limited; while eight private peers operate in the broader sector—including Elroy Air, Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, and Archer Aviation—the same-stage peer set is narrow, with only one direct comparable identified. No public benchmarks exist for meaningful valuation triangulation.

Given the sparse peer data, stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach. Using total capital raised ($40M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement yields an implied valuation of $76M. This accounts for expected value creation between rounds while remaining grounded in capital history rather than speculative growth assumptions.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $65M (low) to $87M (high), with a median of $76M. This range reflects standard variance around the single methodological anchor. Key uncertainties include the absence of sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comps to validate the 1.9x multiplier against market comparables, revenue or unit-economics data for the target, and relative competitive positioning within the autonomous systems landscape. A fuller valuation framework would require either narrower peer identification or additional company-specific operational metrics.
